name: Siloam inscription
description: A Hebrew inscription carved inside the water tunnel under Jerusalem's City of David. It tells how two teams of diggers, cutting from opposite ends, met in the middle.
significance: The tunnel that 2 Kings 20:20 and 2 Chronicles 32:30 credit to King Hezekiah is real and can still be walked through today.
authenticity_note: Most scholars date it to Hezekiah's reign; a few argue for a later date.
museum: Istanbul Archaeology Museums
image_credit: Picture taken by deror avi on July 2005.

name: Temple Warning inscription
description: A stone slab with a Greek warning that non-Jews must not pass the barrier around the Temple's inner courts, on pain of death.
significance: The Temple barrier that the historian Josephus describes was real. It helps explain the riot in Acts 21, when Paul was accused of bringing a Greek into the Temple.
museum: Istanbul Archaeology Museums

name: Caiaphas ossuary
description: A decorated limestone bone box found in a family tomb south of Jerusalem's Old City. One inscription reads "Joseph son of Caiaphas."
significance: Likely the burial box of the high priest's family. The Gospels name Caiaphas as the high priest at Jesus' trial.
authenticity_note: The box is accepted as genuine. Most scholars link it to the high priest Caiaphas; a few think the name could belong to another family.
museum: Israel Museum, Jerusalem

name: James ossuary
description: A limestone bone box inscribed "James, son of Joseph, brother of Jesus." It came from a private collector, so where it was found is unknown.
significance: Not evidence. If the whole inscription is genuine, it would be the earliest mention of Jesus on an object, but that is disputed.
authenticity_note: The box itself is ancient. Experts disagree on whether the words "brother of Jesus" are original. In 2012 an Israeli court cleared its owner of forgery, but said that did not prove the inscription genuine.

name: Magdala Stone
description: A carved stone block found inside a synagogue at Magdala, on the Sea of Galilee. It shows a seven-branched menorah.
significance: Galilean towns had synagogues in Jesus' time, as the Gospels describe when he taught in them (Mark 1:39).

name: Pilate Stone
description: A limestone block found in the Roman theater at Caesarea. Its Latin inscription names Pontius Pilate as prefect of Judea and records a building he dedicated to the emperor Tiberius.
significance: Pontius Pilate was a real Roman governor of Judea, as the Gospels say.
museum: Israel Museum, Jerusalem

name: Capernaum synagogue
description: The ruins of a white limestone synagogue at Capernaum. It was built centuries after Jesus, on top of older black basalt walls.
significance: Capernaum was a real Jewish town on the Sea of Galilee. Some excavators date the basalt walls under the synagogue to the 1st century, the time of the synagogue in Mark 1:21.
authenticity_note: The building is genuine. Whether the basalt walls beneath it belong to the synagogue Jesus knew is debated.
